original_test_intent: Install the approved Linux Server GUI build through IPv4 PXE, reboot into a workable system and verify event logs contain no unexplained issues.
original_method: Agent validates the isolated PXE/DHCP/TFTP/HTTP environment and collects logs; qualified operator selects the exact PXE boot and controls target, partition, package/GUI, credential and reboot decisions.
manual_activity: User approves isolated PXE scope, signed artifacts and wipe target; qualified operator selects PXE/KVM and supervises the destructive Linux GUI installation and reboot.
required_inputs: Exact DUT MAC/NIC/BMC identity, IPv4/VLAN/DHCP/TFTP/HTTP topology and isolated scope
Signed/checksummed bootloader, kernel, initrd, installer image and repository
Approved PXE config or guarded answer file plus package/GUI/driver baseline
Stable target disk/partition/wipe/boot policy and non-target exclusions
Qualified operator, KVM/OOB, backup/recovery and known-event allowlist
safety_requirements: Prove PXE offer is bound to the exact MAC/host on an isolated network
Validate every artifact/config checksum before boot
Confirm stable disk identity at installer before partition/format
Stop on wrong DHCP client/server, target ambiguity, artifact/install/boot/event/power/BMC fault or recovery loss
Restore boot order and remove temporary PXE/DHCP authorization afterward
agent_execution_scope: Validate isolated service/config/artifact readiness and capture DHCP/TFTP/HTTP logs
Correlate exact client MAC with PXE stages
Do not broaden DHCP scope, trigger unverified reimage, select disks, enter secrets or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve network scope, artifacts, target/package/GUI and recovery
Provide qualified operator and own destructive install/recovery
Review PXE, install, reboot and event evidence to decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Network/service checks can support PXE, but no generic command safely proves exact-client boot or controls the destructive interactive install.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Perform read-only preflight of the exact MAC reservation and signed artifact chain, capture per-stage server logs, then let the operator control KVM boot/install and final PXE cleanup.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: IPv4 PXE boot, Linux Server GUI installation, event review and source timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind one MAC/host to a signed PXE artifact chain and exact disk target, preserve DHCP-through-installer evidence, then restore normal boot/network state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds network blast-radius, artifact, target and cleanup controls without replacing the operator-supervised install.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: PXE service validation/logging may be automated; destructive installer and visual GUI acceptance remain supervised.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A mis-scoped DHCP/PXE service can affect other hosts, and unattended files may silently choose disks unless guarded.

project_override_considerations: Only an approved isolated PXE segment/reservation and pinned artifact chain may be used; shared DHCP or wildcard/autoinstall configuration is prohibited unless explicitly governed.
expected_evidence: Critical approval and exact host/MAC/NIC/BMC/network map
Signed PXE artifact/config/answer-file checksums and server versions
DHCP lease/offer, TFTP/HTTP requests and exact-client boot/KVM evidence
Installer/package/GUI/reboot health and complete OS/BMC event evidence
PXE/boot cleanup, known-event triage, recovery readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define IPv4 PXE Linux Server GUI installation and post-reboot/event acceptance.

blocked_analysis.analysis: PXE topology/artifacts, target policy, operator and recovery are supplyable execution prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Constrains PXE to one verified client and signed artifact chain, protects destructive disk selection and makes service/install/cleanup traceable.
independent_technical_reasoning: PXE begins before the OS and a rogue or broad DHCP offer can redirect multiple machines, while an answer file can wipe a disk without another prompt. Therefore evidence must bind the exact NIC MAC through DHCP, bootloader, kernel/initrd and installer target, and completion must include restored boot order and removed temporary authorization.
